newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Short position rolled forward in BP.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Short position rolled forward in BP.

text.p: UK stock options business was bolstered in part by tomorrow's October expiry, dealers said.

As a result one of the larger deals was in British Petroleum where a short position was rolled forward and it involved buying back 500 October 600 calls at 89p and selling 500 January 700 calls at 33p.

Profit from the January calls will accrue from a combination of option time decay and low share price volatility. For maximum profit at the January expiry date, the underlying shares need to stay below 700p.
By 1430 GMT, BP shares were down 9-1/2p to 686p.

Over in aero-engine manufacturer Rolls-Royce the main trade was a diagonal bear spread established by selling 250 November 220 calls at 32p and buying 250 February 260 calls at 12p for a net credit of 22p.
For maximum profit by November expiry, Rolls-Royce shares need to fall to 220p when the short calls will be worthless and the spread will shrink.
The February calls will still have value and these may then be sold if desired, but the strategy may have been employed as a means of owing the longer-dated calls at a reduced price.
Losses will arise if the shares go up owing to the spread -- the difference between the option premiums -- widening.
The chief deal in automotive components group LucasVarity was from a buyer of 775 November 260 calls at 6p. The underlying shares gained 4-1/2p to 254-1/2p.
